line: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 Bc5 d4 exd4 Nxd4 O-O Be2 Re8 Bg5 h6 Bh4 g5 Bg3 Nxe4
teaches: A pin on your king's knight is only as strong as the tactics keeping it there. When the pawns have pushed the pinning bishop to a square where the knight's capture in the centre attacks it, the pin is over — count everything the capture hits before dismissing it as impossible.
explains: The knight has taken on e4 and attacks two pieces from there: the bishop on g3 that was doing the pinning, and the knight on c3. The move looked forbidden while the pin stood; the pawn advances changed the geometry, and now it wins material or the initiative whichever way the opponent answers.
